name: verbatim_double.jsonnet
why: The corpus contains no verbatim string at all, so neither verbatim path is graded by it. Doubled quotes are resolved here and put back by the unparser.

name: verbatim_single.jsonnet
why: The single-quoted verbatim path, likewise ungraded by the corpus.

name: verbatim_junk.jsonnet
why: Upstream formats the offending rune with %v, which prints its numeric value rather than the character.

name: unterminated_single.jsonnet
why: No corpus file provokes a lexer error, so every message below is ungraded by it.

name: unterminated_in_object.jsonnet
why: The same error with a non-trivial column, which is what the parse-error fixture pins.

name: bad_character.jsonnet
why: A character that starts no token at all.

name: number_underscores.jsonnet
why: Separators are dropped from the token data, so the formatter writes 1000 where the author wrote 1_000.

name: number_exponents.jsonnet
why: The accepting paths through the state machine, not just the rejecting ones.

name: operator_plus_run.jsonnet
why: The wind-back reads its deciding character once and never reassigns it, so a run of + cannot form one operator.

name: operator_multi_symbol.jsonnet
why: And a multi-symbol operator that does not end in one of + - ~ ! $ survives intact.

name: operator_ends_with_bang.jsonnet
why: Wind-back again, on an operator that genuinely ends with a forbidden character.

name: dollar.jsonnet
why: $ reaches the lexer through the operator path and is then re-labelled.

name: tab_indent.jsonnet
why: A tab counts as 8 spaces of indent and nothing downstream recovers it.

name: mixed_tab_space_indent.jsonnet
why: Spaces then a tab, which is the ill-advised case the lexer comments on.

name: crlf.jsonnet
why: \r is consumed as whitespace and contributes no indent, which is half of why a CRLF file does not round-trip.

name: comment_paragraph.jsonnet
why: First on its line, so a paragraph.

name: comment_line_end.jsonnet
why: After a token on the same line, so a line end carrying the comment.

name: comment_trailing_whitespace.jsonnet
why: Trailing horizontal whitespace is stripped at lex time and never restored.

name: c_comment_interstitial.jsonnet
why: One line, so it flows after the token it follows.

name: c_comment_paragraph.jsonnet
why: More than one line, so a paragraph — and this is where the dead allStar hack lives.

name: c_comment_star_lhs.jsonnet
why: Every continuation line begins with *, which is exactly what allStar claims to handle — and it still does not fire, because the first line begins with the comment's own /.

name: blank_line_run.jsonnet
why: Blank lines become a count, and the indent is whatever follows the last newline.

name: text_block.jsonnet
why: Both indents are recorded and the unparser reproduces them verbatim.

name: text_block_chomp.jsonnet
why: |||- drops the final newline.

name: text_block_blank_lines.jsonnet
why: Leading and interior blank lines, which are handled before and inside the indent loop respectively.

name: text_block_term_indent.jsonnet
why: The closing ||| may be indented less than the body, and that indent is kept separately.

name: eof_fodder.jsonnet
why: Final whitespace is discarded, so a trailing comment lands on the end-of-file token and nothing else does.

name: empty.jsonnet
why: An empty file still produces an end-of-file token.

name: only_whitespace.jsonnet
why: And whitespace alone produces no fodder, because final whitespace is discarded.
